The square gets its name from the nearby Santuario de la Victoria, the patron saint of Malaga, but it is also known as the Monkey Garden because it once housed a cage with monkeys in the center of the garden; one of them was called "Perico". Alongside this, Pedregalejo has become the best neighborhood in Malaga, combining all the services along with the beach, the unbeatable nightlife by the sea, and tradition. In fact, the house where you are going to stay was built around 1945. It is one of the first bourgeois houses in the neighborhood. A 1983 renovation stripped it of its initial style, but we have renovated it in its entirety, inspired by the traditional houses of Malaga, updating the style, cleaning its forms but maintaining the materials traditionally used in the area. neighborhood_overview: Carranque: A Historic and Residential Neighborhood in Málaga Carranque is a residential neighborhood located in the Cruz de Humilladero district of Málaga. Built in the 1950s, it features a mix of modest single-family homes and low-rise apartment buildings. Originally named Barriada de Francisco Franco, the neighborhood was developed under the initiative of Bishop Herrera Oria and designed by architects Juan Jáuregui and Eduardo Burgos. A Neighborhood with Agricultural Roots The area where Carranque now stands was once part of the Hacienda Carranque, an agricultural estate that cultivated cereals, almond trees, olive groves, and Muscat grape vineyards. The neighborhood's construction was sponsored by the Sagrado Corazón de Jesús Charitable Society of Málaga, and later, RENFE (the Spanish railway company) contributed by building housing for its workers.
